turns.content: Let p be parallax and r distance. If the count density per unit parallax scales as p^-5 and p=k/r, rewrite the p^-5 factor as a power of r.
Differentiate p=k/r with respect to r and give the magnitude of the Jacobian |dp/dr|.
Write the change-of-variables relation between density per unit parallax and density per unit distance, including the Jacobian |dp/dr|.
Combine the parallax-density factor p^-5 with the Jacobian |dp/dr| to obtain the distance-space power law.
State the resulting density-per-unit-distance scaling as a power of r.
State the units of the distance-space density and explain what the interval dr represents.
Report the final distance-space scaling and show how it follows from the parallax density and Jacobian.
